newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- FACTORY OUTPUT PUSHES AHEAD

The latest purchasing managers' survey from the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply says factory exports orders increased in April, but at their slowest rate for almost a year. But despite the weakness of export orders -- due in part to the strength of the pound -- activity in the UK manufacturing sector accelerated in April due to growing domestic consumer demand.
-- MILLENNIUM TIME BOMB THREATENS GLOBAL TELECOMS

Telecoms operators in the UK and US are concerned that counterparts in other parts of the world are not preparing for the so-called 'millennium bomb' -- the inability of devices with computer chips to deal with the date change to the year 2000. The operators have warned that failure by overseas companies to deal with the problem could make it impossible to connect some international telecoms traffic after the turn of the century.
-- SECOND SUITOR FOR APV AS SHARES RISE 50 PER CENT IN WEEK

APV, the British-based process equipment maker, has said it has received its second bid approach in the past week. Opinion in the City is that the second approach was made by the German company GEA, one of APV's largest rivals. GEA is understood to have said that if a bid was made for APV, it would also take a closer interest in its UK rival. Shares in APV closed 5p higher on Thursday at 92p and have risen some 50 percent over the week.
-- EU CHERRY TREE BAN MAY BLIGHT BUDDING TRADE LINKS

Trade between the European Union and Japan could be damaged by an EU ban on imports of Japanese cherry trees. The ban was imposed -- without objection -- in 1993 on health grounds, but later customs officials in Austria admitted that there was no evidence the trees had caused harm to EU plant life. Now Japan has asked the European Commission to lift the ban.
-- ASDA HANDS ITS COMPUTING WORK TO IBM

Supermarket chain Asda ASDA.L is to transfer all its internal computing work to International Business Machines . The 200 million stg deal is one of the largest outsourcing agreements to date in the UK. Asda chief executive Allan Leighton said he was confident the deal would not encounter the problems met by British Steel, which pulled out of talks with IBM for a 350 million stg outsourcing contract over concerns the U.S. group could not meet its commercial requirements.
-- TV CHIEF CALLS FOR SINGLE REGULATORY BODY

The chief executive of the Independent Television Commission, the commercial television regulator, has called for the establishment of a single regulatory body for UK television. Peter Rogers said the new regulator would replace the present range of bodies with overlapping responsibilities, including the separate bodies for commercial television, the BBC, and the Welsh fourth channel. The call also comes in anticipation of an increasing number of television channels and rapid changes in technology.
-- MOBILE PHONE COMPANIES PLAY THEIR LOYALTY CARDS

Mobile phone companies are turning increasingly to tie-ups with companies offering compatible services in a bid to stay ahead of competition in the market. The trend is to offer additional services such as Cellnet's facilities for Barclaycard customers, which reward the loyalty of mobile phone subscribers. In the case of Cellnet, the alliance with Barclaycard has reduced the 'churn' rate of the mobile phone operator to just 5 percent, compared to an average at least four times higher.
-- INTRANETS 'TO DWARF INTERNET BY 2000'
An independent report prepared for British Telecom

has predicted that at least four out of 10 British businesses will be running a corporate intranet by 2002. The claim is based on 1,000 interviews with British companies, and supports the consensus within the IT industry that the global market for intranet technologies will dwarf the Internet by the millennium.
-- EQUANT PICKS NEW EUROPEAN PRESIDENT

Howard Ford, former managing director of UK mobile phone company Cellnet, has been appointed European president of Equant Network Services, the world's biggest data communications network. Equant is co-owned with airline network Sita and it provides services to multinational services on a commercial basis. Equant is hoping for revenues of one billion dollars by January 1999 and is expected top undergo flotation before 2000.
-- CAPITAL SPENDING FALLS AT ROYAL DUTCH/SHELL

Anglo-Dutch oil company Royal Dutch/Shell has reported a lower than expected first quarter capital expenditure of 1.4 billion stg, the lowest in three years. The company had pledged to draw down its 8.9 billion stg cash reserve by investing in new projects. RDS increases in exploration, spending and production offset reductions in refining and chemicals. Analysts are surprised at the announcement, but warn against jumping to conclusions for only one quarter.
